subject: Post-demo: regional latency evaluation & competitive test plan
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya@saasco.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-06T15:12:00Z
Subject: Post-demo: regional latency evaluation & next tests

Hi Maya,

Thanks again for the call earlier — really useful to hear where latency and residency are creating friction for your EU & West-coast customers. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

What we heard:
- You want a side-by-side that measures p50/p95 latency and token throughput across regions (US East, US West, EU West) for your conversational inference workload.
- You’ll want a comparison vs the hyperscaler endpoints you currently use (Bedrock / Vertex) for the same prompt set.
- Data residency constraint: EU customer data must not be persisted outside EU for the EU tenant.

Our proposal (attached: redwood-regional-test-plan.pdf + perf matrix):
1) Run a 2h run per region using your representative prompt set (you said ~1.2k requests/min peak).
2) Measure p50/p95 latency, cold-start, throughput at 1/5/10 concurrent clients, and token cost.
3) Compare same tests against the hyperscaler endpoints you nominate (we can coordinate with you for credentials or run using publicly available endpoints where possible).
4) For EU-resident customers we recommend using Redwood Private or our EU-hosted tenant; for the hosted test we can keep payloads masked and purge logs immediately if that helps get the test greenlit.

Ask from you:
- Confirm the prompt set (upload link or we can pull from the S3 you mentioned).
- Whitelist these IPs for the test window: see attached ip-whitelist.txt.
- Confirm which hyperscaler endpoints you want included (AWS Bedrock, GCP Vertex, any others).

If that all looks good I’ll schedule the runs for next week (Tue/Wed window) and loop in Camila for the benchmark automation.

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

---
Attachments referenced: redwood-regional-test-plan.pdf, redwood-perf-matrix.xlsx
From: Maya Singh <maya@saasco.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit@saasco.com>, SaaSCo - Platform Team <platform@saasco.com>
Date: 2026-07-07T09:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: regional latency evaluation & next tests

Thanks Rachel — appreciate the clear plan.

A few clarifications from our side:
- We can share the canonical prompt set and a redacted customer payload sample; I’ll upload to the S3 bucket and DM you the link today.
- Hyperscaler comparison: please include AWS Bedrock (we use Anthropic/Claude & Amazon_llm variants) and Google Vertex (we have a Vertex LLM endpoint). If you can also include an instance of OpenAI API with comparable model (for price/latency baseline) that would be great.
- Data residency: for production EU customers we require data-at-rest to remain in EU. For the test we can accept masked/pseudonymized payloads, but we need confirmation you will purge logs within 24 hours and not replicate EU payloads to US services.

One more ask — can you show how Redwood’s fallback/routing behaves when a region is unavailable? We’d like to see a simulated outage of eu-west1 and confirm whether requests are routed to another region, and what metadata of the request (IP/region) is retained in logs.

If you can confirm the purge policy and routing behavior we’ll sign off on the test window.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Singh
VP Platform Engineering, SaaSCo

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-07-07T13:30:00Z
Subject: RE: Post-demo: regional latency evaluation & next tests

+1 on the plan. A few implementation notes from the SE/benchmarking side: 

- Test matrix we should run (I added to competitive-test-scripts.sh):
  * Regions: us-east1, us-west1, eu-west1
  * Endpoints: Redwood-hosted (regional), Redwood-hosted (regional) + fallback policy, AWS Bedrock, GCP Vertex, OpenAI (as baseline)
  * Metrics: p50/p95/p99, cpu/GPU utilization where available, cold-start latency (first request after 15m idle), tokens per second, per-token cost estimate.
- For Bedrock/Vertex/OpenAI we’ll hit your existing endpoints; let us know if you prefer us to run from your account or ours. Running from your VPC/egress will reflect real routing; running from our infra gives consistent client conditions.
- Regarding EU data residency: for the hosted test we can 1) pseudonymize payloads before logging 2) set log retention to 1 hour and purge via our retention job 3) isolate eu-west1 logs to EU storage — I’ll have Camila confirm the retention/purge script and include the exact S3/GCS bucket names in the run report.
- Fallback simulation: we can do a controlled outage by disabling the eu-west1 route for 10m and show the routing decision and resulting latency delta. That will include trace IDs for correlation.

I attached the scripts and a small list of presigned S3 links to collect results. Once Maya confirms the prompt set we can schedule runs for Tue 2026-07-14 03:00-07:00 UTC (low traffic for them) or Wed 04:00-08:00 UTC.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Maya — quick confirmations and logistics so we can lock the window: 

1) Test window: Tuesday 2026-07-14 03:00-07:00 UTC (we’ll run each region sequentially during that block). Please confirm and we’ll send calendar invites.
2) IPs to whitelist (attached ip-whitelist.txt) — these are the run agents that will call your endpoints.
3) Data residency/purge: per Marcus — for the hosted run we will pseudonymize payloads client-side, redact PII server-side, and run a retention purge that deletes logs and traces within 1 hour of the run completion. For production EU customers we recommend Private deployment; but for evaluation the above should meet your compliance gating. I attach the EU retention excerpt as a snippet in the Drive link.
4) Hyperscaler comparison: we will include AWS Bedrock, GCP Vertex, and OpenAI baseline unless you tell us otherwise. If you want us to run from your account we’ll need short-lived credentials or an endpoint URL + API key.
5) Fallback test: we will simulate eu-west1 outage for a 10-minute window during the run and capture routing traces & how the request metadata is handled.

Next steps for you (Maya / Platform Team):
- Upload prompt set to the S3 you mentioned or provide a shared Drive link by EOD Mon 2026-07-13.
- Confirm whether we should run hyperscaler tests from your endpoints or ours.
- Whitelist ip list and confirm acceptance of the 1-hour purge policy for this evaluation.

I’ll send the calendar invite once you confirm the window. Looking forward to this — should be a good apples-to-apples data set for your architecture review.

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
